001: How are your preparations going for next week's client presentation?
I've finished the first draft, but I feel the data section isn't solid enough yet.
Then we can double-check the latest market report.
Good idea, I'll organize the relevant data this afternoon.
Do you want me to review the logic of your slides?
That would be great, your opinion is really helpful to me.
002: Where should the focus of this presentation be?
I think we should highlight the core competitiveness of our product.
Then do we need to analyze the competitors' situation in detail?
Just mention it briefly, the focus should still be on our advantages.
Got it, then I'll trim down that part of the content.
Yes, that way the overall pace of the presentation will be tighter.
003: How do you plan to open to grab the client's attention?
I want to use an industry statistic to lead into our solution.
That's a good approach, it can quickly capture their interest.
Do you think it's better to start with data or with a case study first?
I think data is more convincing, what do you think?
That makes sense, then I'll use the data as my opening.
004: How long is appropriate to keep the presentation?
The client gave us thirty minutes, and I plan to speak for twenty-five minutes.
That leaves five minutes for questions, which is well arranged.
I'm still worried that too much content might make us run over time.
You can do a rehearsal first to see the actual duration.
Okay, I'll do a full practice run tonight.
005: Are you ready to answer the client's tough questions?
I've listed some possible questions, but it's not comprehensive enough.
Do you want me to play the client and do a mock session with you?
That would be great, that way I can get used to it in advance.
How about we find a meeting room this afternoon to practice?
No problem, I'll go over the materials once more first.
006: How do you plan to handle the visual effects for this presentation?
I plan to use more charts and less text.
That's the right direction, charts are more intuitive than text.
But I'm not sure which type of chart is the most suitable.
Use a line chart to show trends, and a bar chart to compare data.
Okay, I'll redesign it based on that approach.
007: Does your presentation script need to be translated into an English version?
There are foreign executives on the client's side, so we really do need to prepare it.
Then I can help you contact a colleague from the translation department.
That's great, I'm afraid my own translation might not be accurate with the technical terms.
Don't worry, they have a lot of experience handling business documents.
Then I'll leave it to you, is there still enough time?
008: What preparations do we need to make the day before the presentation?
It's best to go to the venue in advance to test the equipment.
Right, the projector and microphone definitely need to be checked beforehand.
We also need to confirm that the backup files are all in place.
I'll prepare a USB drive for you, and also save a cloud backup.
That's so thoughtful of you, now I can feel at ease.
009: What do you think is the biggest challenge of this presentation?
It should be how to make the client believe our solution is feasible.
Then have you prepared any specific success cases?
There are two cases from similar projects, and the results were quite good.
Then focus on those two cases to strengthen the persuasiveness.
Okay, I'll flesh out the case study section a bit more.
010: After the presentation, what follow-up do we need to do?
We should prepare a detailed proposal document to send to the client.
Then I'll organize the key points from the presentation into a document.
Good, it's best to also include our contact information.
No problem, I'll send it out on the same day the presentation ends.
That way the client can see our proposal in a timely manner.
